narrative: Material PL1__M4DCBDE4 exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=0.30) across 237 working days with no detectable linear trend, making a stable continuous-review (r,Q) policy appropriate. Lead times average 5.43 working days with moderate stability (CV=0.23), requiring a safety stock of 3,669 units to achieve the 95% service level — compared to the current SAP safety stock of zero. The EOQ-optimised order quantity of 15,210 units (constrained by MOQ=2,520) reduces annual ordering frequency and total costs by 60% versus the current policy while remaining within the 20,229-unit storage capacity.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Moderate and non-intermittent demand (non-zero fraction = 1.0, CV=0.30) combined with a binding MOQ and measurable lead-time variability makes the classic (r,Q) model the most appropriate choice. It balances ordering cost efficiency via EOQ against buffer requirements driven by demand and lead-time uncertainty, without requiring simulation or complex multi-echelon modelling.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (20,229 units) exceeds safety_stock + order_quantity (18,879 units) by 1,350 units — a slim margin of ~7%. Any upward revision to safety stock (e.g. due to demand spikes or longer lead times) could breach the cap, requiring a corresponding reduction in order quantity, which would increase ordering frequency and cost.
